## the sign-in, A
⚠️  LARGE PAGES NEED A NEW SIGN-IN
=================================
The security policy gives 'Lock pages in memory' (SeLockMemoryPrivilege) to PC\owner, the account TMR runs as,
but this sign-in began before it did: a program gets the rights its account had at sign-in, so signing
out and back in brings it (Windows needn't restart).

Choose your preferred action:
  A) Exit TMR, then sign out and back in, or restart Windows (RECOMMENDED for optimal performance)
  B) Continue with standard 4KB pages this time (~5-10% slower, so less memory stress)

Enter your choice (A/B): 
✅ Sign out and back in (or restart Windows), then run TMR again: it then uses large pages.

To sign out: Start Menu → your account → Sign out
To restart:
  • Windows: shutdown /r /t 0
  • Or use Start Menu → Power → Restart

TMR will exit now.

## the sign-in, B
⚠️  LARGE PAGES NEED A NEW SIGN-IN
=================================
The security policy gives 'Lock pages in memory' (SeLockMemoryPrivilege) to PC\owner, the account TMR runs as,
but this sign-in began before it did: a program gets the rights its account had at sign-in, so signing
out and back in brings it (Windows needn't restart).

Choose your preferred action:
  A) Exit TMR, then sign out and back in, or restart Windows (RECOMMENDED for optimal performance)
  B) Continue with standard 4KB pages this time (~5-10% slower, so less memory stress)

Enter your choice (A/B): 
⚠️  Continuing with standard 4KB pages (minpage=regular maxpage=regular for this run).
   Performance impact: ~5-10% slower than large pages
   Every test still runs and every pattern is still checked, but slower
   memory traffic is less stress, so marginal errors that only appear at
   full bandwidth may go undetected

💡 TIP: Sign out and back in, then run TMR again, for optimal performance

## the sign-in through a group, under UAC on a domain PC, A
⚠️  LARGE PAGES NEED A NEW SIGN-IN
=================================
The security policy gives 'Lock pages in memory' (SeLockMemoryPrivilege) to BUILTIN\Administrators, a group PC\owner is in,
but this sign-in began before it did: a program gets the rights its account had at sign-in, so signing
out and back in brings it (Windows needn't restart).
After the next sign-in TMR has it in every run, run as administrator or not.
This PC is in a domain: a domain Group Policy that sets this right replaces a local grant.

Choose your preferred action:
  A) Exit TMR, then sign out and back in, or restart Windows (RECOMMENDED for optimal performance)
  B) Continue with standard 4KB pages this time (~5-10% slower, so less memory stress)

Enter your choice (A/B): 
✅ Sign out and back in (or restart Windows), then run TMR again: it then uses large pages.

To sign out: Start Menu → your account → Sign out
To restart:
  • Windows: shutdown /r /t 0
  • Or use Start Menu → Power → Restart

TMR will exit now.

## the grant, A
⚠️  LARGE PAGES NEED THE 'LOCK PAGES IN MEMORY' RIGHT
====================================================
TMR runs as PC\owner, and neither it nor a group it is in has this right (SeLockMemoryPrivilege).
As Administrator, TMR can grant it: whoever gets it keeps it until it is removed (tmr.exe
--remove-large-pages), and it takes effect at their next sign-in.

Choose your preferred action:
  A) Grant it to PC\owner, exit TMR, then sign out and back in (RECOMMENDED for optimal performance)
  B) Continue with standard 4KB pages this time, granting nothing (~5-10% slower, so less memory stress)
  Q) Quit TMR, granting nothing
Or grant it to a group PC\owner is in, then exit TMR and sign out and back in:
  1) BUILTIN\Administrators
  2) BUILTIN\Users  ⚠️
  3) Everyone  ⚠️
  ⚠️  BROAD, use with caution: most or all accounts are in it, and any program of any of these accounts can then lock RAM away from Windows.

Enter your choice (A, B, Q or 1-3): 
🔧 Granting it to PC\owner...

## the administrator's, A
⚠️  LARGE PAGES NEED TMR RUN AS ADMINISTRATOR
============================================
TMR runs as PC\owner without the right large pages need, 'Lock pages in memory' (SeLockMemoryPrivilege).
Only TMR run as administrator can set them up: Run as administrator (right-click TMR), or
tmr.exe --setup-large-pages from a console run as administrator.

Choose your preferred action:
  A) Exit TMR, to run it as administrator (RECOMMENDED for optimal performance)
  B) Continue with standard 4KB pages this time (~5-10% slower, so less memory stress)

Enter your choice (A/B): 
✅ Run TMR as administrator to set up large pages. TMR will exit now.


## the administrator's under UAC, B
⚠️  LARGE PAGES NEED TMR RUN AS ADMINISTRATOR
============================================
TMR runs as PC\owner without the right large pages need, 'Lock pages in memory' (SeLockMemoryPrivilege).
Only TMR run as administrator can set them up: Run as administrator (right-click TMR), or
tmr.exe --setup-large-pages from a console run as administrator.
You sign in as an administrator: run TMR as administrator once to grant it; after the next sign-in it has it in every run.

Choose your preferred action:
  A) Exit TMR, to run it as administrator (RECOMMENDED for optimal performance)
  B) Continue with standard 4KB pages this time (~5-10% slower, so less memory stress)
